html:
A civil war that began with an army mutiny on 19 September 2002 and split Ivory Coast between a rebel-held north, run from Bouake, and the government of Laurent Gbagbo in the south.

The rebels, later called the New Forces, drew on northerners angered by ivoirite. French troops and a United Nations force held a buffer zone between the sides. Peace deals in 2003 and the Ouagadougou agreement of 2007 brought rebel leader Guillaume Soro into government, but the country stayed divided. The war ruined the cocoa economy of the north and the region's main port city, Abidjan, lost business. Footballer Didier Drogba became a voice for peace. It led into the 2010 crisis.
sum: A civil war that began with an army mutiny on 19 September 2002 and split Ivory Coast between a rebel-held north, run from Bouake, and the government of Laurent Gbagbo in the south.
